title: Automated Credential Lifecycle for FinTech Microservices
business: A high-growth FinTech firm managing distributed microservices that require frequent access to third-party payment gateway APIs.
problem: Hardcoded credentials in configuration files lead to security vulnerabilities and manual, error-prone rotation processes that risk service outages.
solution: AWS Secrets Manager provides a centralized vault to store, retrieve, and automatically rotate API keys, decoupling credential management from application code.
steps: Create a secret in AWS Secrets Manager containing the payment gateway API key.
Configure an AWS Lambda function to handle the logic for rotating the third-party API key.
Attach an IAM policy to the application microservice granting permission to call GetSecretValue.
Update application code to fetch the secret at runtime using the AWS SDK instead of reading local files.
Enable automatic rotation in the Secrets Manager console to trigger the Lambda function on a defined schedule.
outcome: The organization achieves improved security posture through automated credential rotation and eliminates the risk of exposed hardcoded secrets in source control.
limitation: Secrets Manager introduces a dependency on an external API call for every secret retrieval, which can increase latency; developers should implement local caching to mitigate this impact.
